query: How does the periodic table organize chemical elements?
title: How the Periodic Table Organizes Elements and Periodic Trends

scenes.title: The Map of the Elements
scenes.narration: The periodic table organizes all chemical elements by atomic number into distinct periods and groups.
scenes.key_takeaway: Elements are organized by atomic number into periods (rows) and groups (columns).

scenes.title: Electronegativity: The Pull for Electrons
scenes.narration: Electronegativity, the pull for shared electrons, increases across periods and decreases down each group.
scenes.key_takeaway: Electronegativity increases across periods and decreases down groups.

scenes.title: Atomic Radius: The Size Gradient
scenes.narration: Conversely, atomic radius shrinks across periods due to nuclear pull, but expands down groups with new shells.
scenes.key_takeaway: Atomic radius decreases left-to-right and increases top-to-bottom.

scenes.title: Predicting Chemical Reactivity
scenes.narration: These predictable periodic trends allow chemists to accurately forecast how any element bonds and reacts.
scenes.key_takeaway: Periodic trends provide predictive power for all chemical interactions.
